acme_infra_jane: Hey team — hitting a weird prod issue on /v1/embeddings. Started ~15:20 UTC, some requests are returning embeddings with shape (1537,) instead of (1536,) and downstream consumers fail with dim mismatch. Only happens when we send batched requests (~8-16 per batch) with dynamic batching enabled. Not seeing it for batch_size=1.

maya-support: Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a couple of example request_ids from the failing requests and the payload shape you're sending? Also, which model and what max_batch_size + dynamic batching settings are you using?

acme_infra_jane: Sure — request ids: rQ_54c1a7, rQ_54c1b0, rQ_54c2f9. Model: text-embed-3-small. Client sends an array of 12 inputs, each short paragraph (~50 tokens). We have max_batch_size=16, dynamic_batching=true in our Dedicated config. Example payload (trimmed):

```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-3-small",
  "input": ["...12 items..."],
  "options": {"max_batch_size": 16}
}
```

acme_infra_jane: Error from our side is: `ValueError: expected 1536, got 1537` when stacking embeddings. Happening ~8% of batches.

maya-support: Thanks. Can you also include the raw response (or at least the first vector) for one of the failing request_ids? Even a truncated first 8 numbers is fine. Also confirming: you saw this start after Friday deploy?

acme_infra_jane: I attached the raw response for rQ_54c1a7 (first vector): `[0.0013, -0.0021, ..., 0.0039]` (length 1537). We did upgrade our client lib Friday but rolled back — issue persisted. We haven't changed model or server config.

maya-support: Understood. I'm escalating to infra/ML to check batching pad/trimming behavior. @chris-ml can you take a look at dynamic batching merge behavior?

chris-ml: Looking. Reproduced locally with a small harness: sending 12 inputs with dynamic batching turned on produced one merged batch where one shard returned a vector with one extra dimension. Logs suggest the KV-cache concat/pack path incorrectly appended an extra padding token vector element when batch length alignment triggered an AVX path. Posting debug log excerpt: 

```
[2026-06-12T15:20:12Z] batch_id=bd_9123 shards=2 merge_step=pack_kv cache_pad=1 pack_len=1536 -> observed_out=1537
[2026-06-12T15:20:12Z] sub_shard=1 pack_op=memcpy len_src=6144 len_dst=6145
```

chris-ml: Looks like a rare off-by-one in the pack_len calculation when a cache padding flag is set (cache_pad=1) and the kernel chooses the AVX-unrolled memcpy. This only shows up when multiple requests of slightly different sequence lengths get merged by dynamic batching and padding is applied per-shard.

sam-oncall: Do we have a short mitigation we can tell the customer? Canary rollback? Temporary config?

chris-ml: Mitigation options: 1) disable dynamic batching for that model (forces each request to be handled independently) 2) set max_batch_size=1 (impractical at scale) 3) route requests to single replica group that uses the scalar memcpy path (we can do a quick sticky policy) 4) quick patch to ensure pack_len is clamped to model_dim before memcpy (low-risk).

maya-support: I'll relay 1 and 3 for immediate mitigation. @acme_infra_jane — can you switch your route to disable dynamic batching for the model for a couple hours while we patch? If you want us to do the routing change from our side, tell us which deployment/route id.

acme_infra_jane: Route id is rd_acme_prod_v2. Can you toggle dynamic batching off for that route? We'll be fine for a few hours. Also please let us know if a server-side fix will require a redeploy.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Rolling config update: disable_dynamic_batching=true on rd_acme_prod_v2 (initiated by maya-support).

maya-support: Done, I flipped the toggle and confirmed no requests are using dynamic batching for rd_acme_prod_v2. Please monitor and report if the dim mismatch reoccurs.

acme_infra_jane: Confirmed — after toggle, no failures in 20m window. Thanks.

chris-ml: I'm preparing a small runtime patch to clamp pack_len and add an assertion in the pack memcpy path. Plan: patch the runtime (C++), unit test with fuzzed sequence lengths, canary deploy to 5% traffic, monitor embedding shape errors and latency. Estimated low-risk and small perf impact.

chris-ml: Patch diff (excerpt):

```diff
- size_t dst_len = computed_pack_len;
- memcpy(dst, src, dst_len * sizeof(float));
+ size_t dst_len = std::min(computed_pack_len, (size_t)model_dim);
+ assert(dst_len <= model_dim);
+ memcpy(dst, src, dst_len * sizeof(float));
+ if (dst_len < model_dim) memset(dst + dst_len, 0, (model_dim - dst_len) * sizeof(float));
```

chris-ml: We'll also add a regression test that constructs two sub-batches with different seq lengths and asserts final tensor dim==model_dim across shards.

sam-oncall: Ops question — will canary cause increased latency? We should watch tail p50/p95. chris-ml: small memcpy clamp shouldn't change asymptotic perf; maybe micro-ns for the assertion path in debug build, but production builds won't assert. Canary at 5% for 30m then 20% for 1h.

maya-support: ETA for first canary?

chris-ml: I'll cut the patch now and request a deploy. ETA ~40m to canary because of CI and packing. I'll post when it's live.

[~36 minutes later]

chris-ml: Canary 5% live at 16:02 UTC. Observability: embedding_shape_mismatch errors dropped to 0 in canary hosts; tail latency unchanged. Posting canary logs snippet: 

```
[2026-06-12T16:02:15Z] canary=5% batch_merge_ok=1200 batch_errors=0
[2026-06-12T16:02:16Z] canary=5% tail_p95=12.3ms baseline_p95=12.0ms
```

chris-ml: Increasing to 20% now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary -> 20% (requested by chris-ml).

chris-ml: 20% steady for 45m, no shape errors. Raising change to full rollout.

deploy-bot: [deploy] rolling -> 100% (requested by chris-ml).

maya-support: Patch rolled to prod. @acme_infra_jane we re-enabled dynamic batching on rd_acme_prod_v2 and verified successful requests. Please confirm you see normal behavior on your side.

acme_infra_jane: Confirmed. No dim mismatches after patch and re-enable. Huge thanks for the quick turnaround.

maya-support: Closing loop: root cause was an off-by-one pack length when padding KV caches during dynamic batching, triggered by an AVX-unrolled memcpy path on a subset of shards. Fix: clamp pack_len to model_dim and zero-pad as needed; added regression tests and canary rollout. If you hit anything else ping us back here. :thumbsup:

acme_infra_jane: Appreciated! One follow-up: can you add an option to surface embedding_shape_mismatch as an alert metric so we can get notified before downstream breaks?

maya-support: Good idea — filing a follow-up ticket to add a customer-visible metric/alert for shape mismatches and a recommended playbook.

chris-ml: Filed: TKT-emb-4321 — add metric, alert, and playbook.

sam-oncall: Marking incident resolved. Will add postmortem summary to /incidents later.
